decisive_items: exploratory laparotomy “showed no mechanical cause of the obstructions”
CT scan showed small-bowel dilation (approximately 23 mm in diameter) consistent with obstruction
A gluten-free diet trialed for 3 months produced no improvement
response.rationale: Recurrent obstructive symptoms with no mechanical cause on laparotomy, small-bowel dilation and megacolon on imaging, and failure of gluten-free diet point to a motility disorder (intestinal pseudo-obstruction). Short bowel syndrome is less likely given no resection history; other candidates lack key supportive features or are contradicted.

rejected.why: No surgical resection or short bowel anatomy; weight loss and vitamin deficiencies are nonspecific and explained by pseudo-obstruction with bacterial overgrowth/malabsorption.
Explicitly no evidence of celiac disease on endoscopy and no response to gluten-free diet.
No protein-losing enteropathy or characteristic endoscopic/histologic findings; vitamin deficiencies alone are insufficient.
Alcohol history is present but does not explain intestinal dilation, megacolon, or absence of mechanical obstruction; symptoms worsened after stopping alcohol.
